recommendation: Keep the fixed commit. It makes the current build's narrative and conformance CodeSystem match the applied Jira resolution and WGM evidence; revisit only if FHIR-I intentionally wants to exclude instant from the transform family despite the issue/minutes naming it.
issue_request: FHIR-40645 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core mapping language. It asked to replace undocumented dateOp target transform parameters with separate date/time parsing operations such as toDate, toTime, toDateTime, and Unix-offset equivalents, using Java-style format strings constrained to features also available in .NET.
initial_application: FHIR-23937 was the predecessor Published tracker and deferred actual dateOp parameter definition to this R6 issue after only changing nearby FHIRPath-context text. PR HL7/fhir#3967, especially dbd826d76742728977c19b819e0ae55b532e9992 and follow-up ed4b1fdd32cbd11f4b3b388e50aaeeece326c3be, removed the narrative dateOp placeholder and added toDateTime/unixToDateTime, toDate/unixToDate, and toTime/unixToTime rows, but did not update CodeSystem/map-transform and did not add instant rows.
additional_context: FHIR-I WGM minutes for 2024-01-30 record date, time, dateTime, and instant conversion, individual functions instead of a return-type parameter, Unix-offset conversion discussion, and a 17-0-1 vote. The linked Zulip thread confirms the FHIR Mapping Language use case for parsing known legacy date/time strings. Build-scope checks showed mapping-language.html is listed in source/hierarchy.xml, StructureMap is active in source/fhir.ini, StructureMap.group.rule.target.transform is required-bound to ValueSet/map-transform, and that value set includes the complete CodeSystem/map-transform.
reconciliation: Added toInstant and unixToInstant to source/mapping-language.html, fixed the adjacent typo introduced in the new date/time format-code paragraph, and replaced the stale dateOp CodeSystem concept in source/structuremap/codesystem-map-transform.xml with toDateTime, unixToDateTime, toInstant, unixToInstant, toDate, unixToDate, toTime, and unixToTime definitions.
